description: Image-Based Code Execution Attack Attackers can craft malicious image files that contain executable code in their metadata or pixel data. When these images are processed, the code could be executed if proper sanitization and isolation aren't in place. An attacker uploads a PNG file with embedded shellcode in its metadata. During image processing, the malicious code is executed within the Lambda environment, potentially leading to data exfiltration or further system compromise.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter
mitreATT&CK: T1204.003 - User Execution: Malicious Image
recommendation: Implement secure image processing in an isolated environment

description: Missing TLS and Certificate Management Without proper TLS configuration and valid certificates, communications between clients and the API/CDN could be intercepted or manipulated through man-in-the-middle attacks. An attacker performing a man-in-the-middle attack could intercept traffic between users and the API Gateway, potentially capturing sensitive data or session tokens.
references: recommendation: Implement ACM and TLS for all endpoints

description: Insufficient Access Controls in S3 Misconfigured bucket policies or IAM roles could allow unauthorized access to private images stored in S3 buckets, bypassing intended access controls. An attacker could exploit overly permissive IAM roles to access private images directly from S3, bypassing the CloudFront distribution and access controls.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket policies
recommendation: Enable S3 encryption and logging

description: Insecure Direct Object References in Image Retrieval The image retrieval endpoint accepts an imageId parameter that could be manipulated to access other users' images if proper authorization checks aren't implemented. An authenticated user modifies the imageId parameter in their request to access images belonging to other users by trying different ID values.

DDoS Vulnerability in API Gateway Attackers could overwhelm the API Gateway with a large number of requests, potentially exhausting Lambda concurrency limits or causing throttling. An attacker launches a distributed denial of service attack against the API endpoints, making the service unavailable to legitimate users.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement AWS Shield and WAF
recommendation: Configure proper throttling and caching

description: Insufficient Logging and Monitoring Without comprehensive logging and monitoring, security incidents might go undetected or be discovered too late for effective response. An attacker performs reconnaissance and eventual data exfiltration while staying undetected due to insufficient logging and monitoring.
references: owaspTop10: A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
recommendation: Implement security monitoring and alerting

description: Sensitive Data Exposure in DynamoDB Sensitive metadata stored in DynamoDB could be exposed through over-privileged IAM roles, improper access patterns, or unencrypted DAX cache. An attacker with access to an over-privileged Lambda function could scan the DynamoDB table to extract sensitive metadata about all users' images.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories
